Linde: Dutch, from the linden or lime tree (linde). Also used as a short form of names ending in -linde, such as Rosalinde.
Loes: Dutch short form of Heloïse or Aloïsa, ultimately from Germanic roots usually explained as 'hale, wide' plus 'wise'; also linked to Louise.
Amin: Arabic, 'trustworthy, faithful'. Also spelled Amine or Ameen; the same root as Amen.
Lucille: French, a diminutive of Lucie, from Latin lux 'light'. Related to Lucia and Lucy.
Nelya: Probably a Slavic or Turkic-area form related to Nelly, itself a short form of Helen or Eleanor. Origin uncertain.
Saja: Arabic, 'cooing of a dove' or 'rhymed prose'. Also spelled Sajaa or Sajah.
Ward: Dutch and English, from Old English weard 'guard, watchman'. In Flanders also sometimes a short form of Edward or Steward.
Leander: Greek, probably 'lion man' or 'man of the people'. In myth, Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to meet Hero.
Ömer: Turkish form of Arabic Umar, probably 'long-lived' or 'flourishing'. Omar is the Arabic form.
Eren: Turkish, 'saint, enlightened person' or 'accomplished one'. Used for boys and sometimes girls.
Richard: Germanic, from ric 'ruler, power' and hard 'brave, hardy'. Brought to Belgium via French and Dutch; Rik and Ricky are short forms.
Janna: Dutch and Scandinavian feminine form of Jan (John), from Hebrew 'God is gracious'. Also a variant of Jana.
Titus: Latin, of uncertain origin, possibly 'title of honour'. Borne by a Roman emperor and a companion of the apostle Paul.
Amadou: West African (Fula, Mandinka), a form of Ahmad or Hamadu, from Arabic 'most praised'. Common in Senegal, Guinea and Mali.
Zaid: Arabic, 'increase, growth, abundance'. Also spelled Zayd or Zaid; a companion of the Prophet Muhammad bore the name.
Theodore: Greek Theodoros, 'gift of God'. Related to Theodoor and Dorian forms; Theo is the usual short form.
Kiara: Italian form of Clara 'bright, clear', also a modern coined name popularised in the 1990s. Also used for the Irish Ciara.
Farah: Arabic, 'joy, happiness'. Common across the Arab world and in Muslim communities in Belgium.
Soline: French, probably a variant of Solène, from Latin sollemnis 'solemn, festive' via the saint Solange. Origin partly uncertain.
Taha: Arabic, the title of the 20th sura of the Qur'an; its meaning is unclear and often read as a mysterious letter pair.
Aicha: Arabic Aisha, 'alive, living'. Name of the Prophet Muhammad's wife; Aicha is the North African spelling.
Marta: Aramaic, 'lady, mistress'. Biblical sister of Lazarus; the Spanish, Italian and Polish form of Martha.
Félice: French form of Felix or Felicia, from Latin felix 'happy, fortunate'.
Rania: Arabic, 'gazing, looking' or 'queen' (from Rani). Popular among Arabic-speaking families.
Mathilde: Germanic, from maht 'might' and hild 'battle'. French and Dutch form; Mathilda and Tilly are variants.
Manou: French pet form of Manuel, Emmanuel or Manon. Also used independently as a modern name.
Asma: Arabic, 'more exalted, higher' or 'more prestigious'. Asma bint Abu Bakr was a companion of the Prophet.
Celia: Latin, from the Roman family name Caelius, perhaps 'heavenly'. Also used as a short form of Cecilia.
Kerem: Turkish, 'generosity, kindness, grace'. Also an old Turkish word for a vineyard-like place, and a folk-tale hero.
Ivan: Slavic form of John, from Hebrew Yochanan 'God is gracious'. Widespread in Russian, Balkan and Slavic communities.
Dalia: Hebrew 'branch' or 'to draw water', also Arabic 'grapevine'. Also an alternative spelling of the flower name Dahlia.
Archibald: Germanic via Scots, from ercan 'genuine' and bald 'bold'. Old-fashioned name now rare in Belgium; Archie is the short form.
Giulio: Italian form of Julius, from Latin Iulius, a Roman family name of uncertain origin, possibly 'youthful'.
Amara: Igbo 'grace', also Latin 'bitter', and Sanskrit 'immortal'. A multi-origin name used in several cultures.
Logan: Scottish and Irish, from a place name and surname meaning 'small hollow'. Used as a given name since the 20th century.
Marthe: French and Dutch form of Martha, from Aramaic 'lady, mistress'. A biblical sister of Lazarus.
Imrane: French spelling of Arabic Imran, from the Qur'anic family of Imran, father of Mary. Meaning debated, perhaps 'prosperous'.
Carla: Italian, German and Spanish feminine form of Carl, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Sana: Arabic, 'brilliance, radiance, splendour'. Also a Persian and Urdu name.
Adriana: Latin, feminine of Adrian, meaning 'from Hadria', a town in northern Italy.
Manel: Catalan short form of Manuel, from Hebrew Immanuel 'God is with us'. Also used in Arabic-speaking North Africa as Manal.
Tyler: English occupational surname, 'tile maker or tiler', from Old English. Used as a given name mainly since the 20th century.
Eleonora: Italian, Dutch and Slavic form of Eleanor; the origin is disputed, perhaps linked to Helen 'torch' or Provençal Aliénor.
Elian: Probably a variant of Elias or Julian, or a Welsh name. Origin uncertain; also a modern coined name.
Zakariya: Arabic form of Zechariah, from Hebrew 'the Lord remembers'. A prophet in the Qur'an and father of John the Baptist.
Léonard: French from Germanic leon 'lion' and hard 'brave, hardy'. Saint Leonard is patron of prisoners.
Dominic: Latin Dominicus, 'belonging to the Lord'. Linked to Saint Dominic, founder of the Dominican Order.
Aris: Greek, short form of Aristotle, Aristides or Ares, with 'best' or 'war god' as possible roots. Also Latvian use.
Hervé: French, from Breton Haerveu, 'battle-worthy' (haer 'battle' plus ve 'worthy'). Saint Hervé was a Breton hermit.
Walt: English short form of Walter, from Germanic wald 'rule' and hari 'army'. Also used on its own.
Édouard: French form of Edward, from Old English ead 'wealth, fortune' and weard 'guard'.
Arnaud: French form of Arnold, from Germanic arn 'eagle' and wald 'rule'.
Thor: Old Norse, 'thunder'. The Norse god of thunder; also a common Scandinavian name.
Estée: French form of Esther, probably from Persian 'star'. Popularised by cosmetics maker Estée Lauder.
Jutta: German, a form of Judith, from Hebrew 'woman of Judea' or 'praised'. Common in Germany and Flanders.
Enola: Likely a modern coined name, famous as the Enola Gay plane; sometimes read as 'alone' spelled backwards. Also possibly Native American. Uncertain.
Romi: Short form of Romy, in turn from Rosemarie or Romola. Also used in Hebrew meaning 'my lofty one'.
Nahil: Arabic, 'one who drinks deeply' or 'receiver of a gift'. Also spelled Nahyl.
Paula: Latin, feminine of Paul, from Paulus 'small, humble'.
Asel: Kazakh and Kyrgyz, 'honey, sweet'. Also a Turkish spelling variant related to Asil. Used in Central Asia.
Willem: Dutch form of William, from Germanic wil 'will, desire' and helm 'helmet, protection'.
Raf: Short form of Raphael or Rafael, from Hebrew 'God has healed'. Also an independent Flemish nickname.
Jenna: English, a variant of Jenny or Jennifer, Cornish form of Guinevere 'white wave, fair one'. Also an Arabic word for paradise.
Vinz: Short form of Vincent, from Latin vincere 'to conquer'. Also used as a standalone nickname.
Ismael: Spanish and French form of Ishmael, from Hebrew 'God hears'. The son of Abraham in the Bible and Qur'an.
Firdaws: Arabic, 'paradise, highest garden', from the Qur'an. Related to Persian-derived word 'paradise'.
Melek: Turkish, 'angel', from Arabic malak. Also a Hebrew form of 'king', melech.
Silas: Latin short form of Silvanus 'of the forest' or Aramaic Saul. Companion of Paul in the New Testament.
Rowan: Irish, from Ruadhán 'little red one', or from the rowan tree. Used for both sexes in English.
Joanne: English and French variant of Joanna or Jeanne, from Hebrew Yochanan 'God is gracious'.
Asiya: Arabic, 'one who tends or heals' or 'sorrowful'. Name of the Pharaoh's wife in Islamic tradition.
Caleb: Hebrew, possibly 'dog' or 'wholehearted'. A faithful spy in the Old Testament.
Jackie: English diminutive of Jack or Jacqueline, from Hebrew Yaakov 'supplanter'.
Isaïah: Hebrew Yeshayahu, 'God is salvation'. A major Old Testament prophet.
Anissa: Arabic, feminine of Anis, 'friendly, close companion'. Also spelled Anisa.
Ophélie: French, from Greek ophelia 'help, aid'. Known from Shakespeare's Hamlet.
Elyas: Variant of Elias, Hebrew Eliyahu 'my God is Yahweh'. Also Arabic Ilyas for the prophet Elijah.
Mylo: Probably a variant of Milo, itself of Germanic or Latin origin, perhaps 'soldier' or 'merciful'. Origin uncertain.
Jérome: Spelling without circumflex of Jérôme, from Greek Hieronymos 'sacred name'. Saint Jerome translated the Bible into Latin.
Tim: Short form of Timothy, from Greek Timotheos 'honouring God'. Also used independently in Dutch.
Jérôme: French form of Jerome, from Greek Hieronymos 'sacred name'. Saint Jerome translated the Bible into Latin.
Miriam: Hebrew, possibly 'beloved', 'bitter' or 'rebellious'; origin uncertain. The sister of Moses; same as Mary.
Elliott: English, from a surname derived from Elias, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'. Also linked to Old English forms.
Cesar: Spanish and Portuguese form of Caesar, a Roman cognomen of uncertain meaning, perhaps 'hairy' or 'blue-grey eyes'.
René: French, from Latin Renatus 'reborn'. Related to Renée in girls.
Alpha: From the first letter of the Greek alphabet, 'first, beginning'. Also used in West African Fula communities, as in Alpha Oumar.
Mahé: French, a Breton form of Matthew via Mathieu. Also linked to a Seychelles island and a coastal town in India.
Ari: Hebrew, 'lion', and also Old Norse 'eagle'. Also a short form of Ariel or Aristotle.
Ishaaq: Arabic form of Isaac, from Hebrew 'he laughs'. A prophet in Islam.
Géraud: French form of Gerald, from Germanic ger 'spear' and wald 'rule'.
Justin: Latin Iustinus, from iustus 'just, fair'. Borne by early saints and Byzantine emperors.
Paulien: Dutch, a form of Pauline, feminine of Paulus, Latin 'small, humble'.
Lorena: Spanish and Italian form of Lorraine, the region of eastern France; ultimately from Lothar-ingia, 'kingdom of Lothair'.
Alan: Celtic, possibly 'little rock' or 'handsome'; of Breton origin. Origin debated.
Leila: Arabic, 'night'. Also Persian 'dark-haired beauty'. Common in Muslim communities.
Liene: Dutch short form of Liesbeth or Eveline, or Latvian from Lienīte. Origin partly uncertain.
Arda: Turkish, 'forest, meadow' or 'successor', and also Persian 'holy'. Used mainly for boys in Turkey.
Maïssa: Arabic Maysa, 'proudly walking, graceful gait'. Also spelled Maissa.
Ninon: French pet form of Anne or Anne-Marie. Made famous by the 17th century courtesan Ninon de Lenclos.
Abigail: Hebrew, 'my father is joy'. A wife of King David in the Old Testament.
Naïla: Arabic, 'one who attains or achieves'. Also spelled Nayla or Nailah.
Isaak: German and Dutch form of Isaac, from Hebrew 'he laughs'.
Hortense: French, from Latin Hortensia, a Roman family name from hortus 'garden'.
Marin: French, from Latin marinus 'of the sea'. Also a Croatian and Romanian name.
Will: English short form of William, from Germanic wil 'will' and helm 'helmet'.
Dean: English, from a surname meaning 'valley' or 'church official'. Also Italian Dino variants.
Louane: Modern French coined name, from Louise combined with Anne, or a variant of Lou-Anne. Popularised by French singer Louane.
Timothée: French form of Timothy, from Greek Timotheos 'honouring God'.
Eric: Old Norse Eiríkr, 'ever ruler' or 'sole ruler'. Used widely in Scandinavia and the Low Countries.
Ilyana: Probably a variant of Iliana or Eliana, feminine of Ilya, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'. Origin uncertain.
Irina: Russian and Romanian form of Irene, from Greek eirene 'peace'.
Minne: Dutch Frisian, a short form of old Germanic names with minne 'love'. Also a Frisian first name.
Soulayman: French spelling of Arabic Sulayman, the Qur'anic form of Solomon, from Hebrew 'peaceful'.
Pia: Latin and Italian, 'pious, devout'. Also used as a short form of Olympia.
Thea: Short form of Dorothea or Theodora, 'gift of God' from Greek. Also Greek 'goddess'.
Leia: Probably a variant of Leah, Hebrew for 'weary' or 'wild cow'. Popularised by Princess Leia in Star Wars.
Ayaan: Somali 'luck, fortune', also Sanskrit and Arabic-region use as 'gift of God' or 'bright'. A multi-origin name.
Jesse: Hebrew Yishai, possibly 'gift' or 'God exists'. The father of King David.
Lenny: English short form of Leonard or Lennox, from Germanic leon 'lion'.
Thalia: Greek, 'flourishing, blooming'. The Muse of comedy.
Tommy: English diminutive of Thomas, from Aramaic 'twin'.
Sepp: Bavarian and Flemish short form of Joseph, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Ema: Slavic, Portuguese and Japanese forms; in Europe a variant of Emma, from Germanic ermen 'whole, universal'.
Zeyneb: Turkish form of Arabic Zaynab, 'fragrant tree' or 'father's adornment'. Daughter of the Prophet Muhammad.
Juna: Probably a modern variant of Juno or Jun, or a short form of Giuliana. Origin uncertain.
Mariama: West African form of Mariam or Maryam, from Hebrew Miriam. Common in Guinea and Senegal.
Inara: Likely modern coined or a Latvian name; also Arabic 'enlightened'. Origin uncertain.
Jul: Flemish short form of Julien or Jules, from Latin Iulius. Also a surname-based short form.
Mohamad: Variant spelling of Muhammad, Arabic 'praised, praiseworthy'.
Abdoulaye: West African French spelling of Abdullah, Arabic 'servant of God'.
Mihra: Likely Persian and Turkish, from Mihr 'sun, love, kindness'. Also Turkish Mihrimah.
Lyzio: Probably a modern variant of Lizio or Lisio; origin uncertain, perhaps from Italian or Belgian coinage.
Nahyl: Variant spelling of Arabic Nahil, 'one who drinks deeply'.
Jason: Greek Iason, 'healer'. The Argonaut leader in myth.
Hajar: Arabic form of Hagar, perhaps 'flight, emigration'. Mother of Ishmael.
Coline: French, a form of Colette or Nicole, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Sirine: Arabic, 'serene, calm', or a form of Syrian. Also Hebrew 'wise woman'.
Emmy: Short form of Emma or Emilia, from Germanic ermen 'whole, universal'.
Issam: Arabic, 'protector, guarantor'. Often used as a first name across the Arab world.
Thélio: Probably a modern French coinage, possibly from Greek Helios 'sun'. Origin uncertain.
Zain: Arabic, 'beauty, grace, goodness'. Also spelled Zayn or Zein.
Ciro: Italian form of Cyrus, from Persian 'sun' or 'throne'. Typical of Naples.
Soraya: Persian, 'Pleiades, jewel'. Also a Spanish and Portuguese form of the Arabic name.
Wolf: Germanic, from wolf, the animal. Often a short form of Wolfgang.
Eliza: Short form of Elizabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Deniz: Turkish, 'sea, ocean'. Used for both boys and girls.
Robert: Germanic, from hrod 'fame' and beraht 'bright'. Common across Europe.
Niene: Frisian and Dutch, a form of Nienke, which is a pet form of Catharina or Nina. Origin partly uncertain.
Jake: English diminutive of Jacob, from Hebrew 'supplanter'.
Kamila: Slavic and Arabic form of Camilla, perhaps 'perfect' in Arabic, or Latin 'young attendant'.
Amos: Hebrew, 'carried by God' or 'burdened'. A minor prophet in the Old Testament.
Louka: French form of Luke or Lukas, from Greek 'man from Lucania'. A modern variant of Luca.
Téo: French and Portuguese short form of Théodore or Mateo, from Greek 'gift of God'.
Elie: French form of Elijah, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Gabriela: Feminine of Gabriel, Hebrew 'God is my strength'.
Lydia: Greek, 'woman from Lydia', a region in Asia Minor. Mentioned in the New Testament.
Luciano: Italian, from Latin Lucianus, 'of Lucius', related to lux 'light'.
Talya: Hebrew, 'dew of God'. Also a Turkish form of Talia.
Luce: French and Italian, from Latin lux 'light'. Short form of Lucie or Lucia.
Tesnim: Arabic Tasnim, 'a spring in Paradise'. Also spelled Tasnim.
Joud: Arabic, 'generosity, bounty'. Also spelled Jud or Jood.
Damir: Slavic and Turkic, 'peace' plus 'world' in Slavic, or 'iron' in Turkic. Common in the Balkans.
Alfie: English diminutive of Alfred, from Old English 'elf counsel'.
Solène: French, from Solemnia, from Latin sollemnis 'solemn, festive'. Saint Solène was a 5th century bishop's mother in Chartres.
Amal: Arabic, 'hope, aspiration'. Also a Hebrew name 'toil' for boys.
Quinn: Irish, from Ó Cuinn, 'descendant of Conn', meaning 'chief' or 'wisdom'. Used for both sexes.
Faye: English, from Old French fae 'fairy', or a short form of Faith. Used since the 19th century.
Tao: Chinese, 'the way, path'. Also used in French-speaking areas as a short form of Théo or Taos.
Linus: Greek, a name from myth, possibly from linen 'flax'. Also the second pope.
Basiel: Flemish form of Basil, from Greek basileios 'royal, kingly'.
Elyna: Variant of Elina or Eline, possibly from Helen 'torch' or Elin, a Scandinavian form of Helen.
Manoa: Polynesian and Hebrew 'rest, tranquil place'. Also a Hawaiian valley name. Rare in Belgium; origin uncertain.
Eyden: Modern English coined name, probably a variant of Aidan or Eden. Origin uncertain.
Qassim: Arabic, 'divider, distributor'. Also spelled Kassim or Qasim.
Esteban: Spanish form of Stephen, from Greek stephanos 'crown, wreath'.
Marco: Italian and Spanish form of Mark, from Latin Marcus, probably linked to Mars.
Samy: French diminutive of Samuel or Sami, from Hebrew 'name of God' or Arabic 'elevated, exalted'.
Korneel: Dutch form of Cornelius, from Latin cornu 'horn'. A Roman family name.
Alban: Latin Albanus, 'from Alba'. The first British martyr, Saint Alban.
Adelina: Germanic, diminutive of Adela, from adal 'noble'.
Matilda: Latinised form of Mathilde, Germanic 'mighty in battle'.
Albane: French feminine of Alban, Latin Albanus, 'from Alba'. Also linked to alba 'white'.
Oumou: West African, a form of Umm or Oumou, from Arabic 'mother'. Common in Guinea and Mali.
Mille: Danish and Norwegian short form of Camilla or Emilie. Also Dutch Mille as a pet name.
Nikodem: Polish form of Nicodemus, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Lander: Flemish, a form of Leander, Greek 'lion man', or from Old English.
Fabian: Latin Fabianus, from the Roman family name Fabius, perhaps 'bean grower'.
Yasin: Arabic, the title of the 36th sura of the Qur'an. Its meaning is uncertain, perhaps two letters.
Manu: Short form of Manuel or Emmanuel, Hebrew 'God is with us'. Also Sanskrit 'man, thinker'.
Annabelle: Combination of Anna, Hebrew 'grace', and belle, French 'beautiful'.
Osman: Turkish form of Arabic Uthman, perhaps 'baby bustard'. Founder of the Ottoman dynasty.
